children: What happened?

A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after warnings emerged that ongoing component supply chain bottlenecks and cleanroom space constraints will restrict semiconductor equipment makers from meeting demand through 2027.

CNBC reported that semiconductor equipment maker Lam Research highlighted during its earnings call that shortages of critical upstream parts and certified cleanroom facilities continue to curb manufacturing velocity.

As detailed by CNBC, cleanrooms are specialized, dust-free environments essential for fabricating microscopic circuitry without microscopic contaminants damaging delicate silicon wafers. When available cleanroom capacity is restricted, chip fabricators cannot readily install new machinery or ramp up production lines, even when customer appetite for chips remains robust, CNBC explained.

Additionally, CNBC noted that lingering supplier bottlenecks mean tool manufacturers struggle to assemble and deliver complex equipment on schedule. While industry leaders are deploying capital to expand production facilities and adjust to evolving structural chip architectures, executive commentary indicates these operational roadblocks will persist into 2027, according to CNBC.

As CNBC highlighted, the realization that physical capacity hurdles may cap near-term revenue realization and tool delivery schedules weighed on investor sentiment across the broader semiconductor manufacturing and equipment space.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

Zooming in on FormFactor (FORM)

FormFactor’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 79 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for FormFactor and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was about 23 hours ago when the stock gained 3.8% on the news that strong demand for artificial intelligence hardware and robust corporate earnings reignited investor optimism across the broader AI technology landscape.

As reported by CNBC, this rally lifted major players across semiconductor manufacturing and cloud computing infrastructure—including AMD, Nvidia, Micron, and Marvell—after SpaceX reported a massive 161% jump in third-quarter revenue. The network noted that investors responded enthusiastically to these results as clear indications that spending on artificial intelligence remains resilient, particularly after SpaceX revealed its AI business grew ninefold to generate $7.56 billion in the quarter. Providing a massive secondary catalyst for the tech-heavy Nasdaq, CNBC reported that Elon Musk announced SpaceX and Tesla have officially formed special committees to discuss a merger between the two companies. As corporate performance numbers demonstrate ongoing investments in technical infrastructure, CNBC observed that market sentiment shifted swiftly back toward the suppliers powering this computing ecosystem, aided heavily by anticipation of Tesla's upcoming earnings report later today.

Ultimately, CNBC highlighted that these sustained capital expenditure commitments and resulting revenues alleviate recent market concerns of an impending AI deceleration, proving that the infrastructure build-out continues to offer a long runway for component designers and infrastructure providers alike.

FormFactor is up 62% since the beginning of the year, but at $95.83 per share, it is still trading 40.1% below its 52-week high of $159.93 from June 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of FormFactor’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $2,581.
